candidates.comment: An address relation between an entity (e.g., organization, person, place) and its physical postal address. Also called physical location, mailing address, street address. Examples: "A company's address is '123 Main St, Anytown'.", "A person's address is 'PO Box 123'.", "The restaurant's address is '456 Oak Ave'."

candidates.label: streetAddress
candidates.comment: A textual representation of the street address component of a postal address. Also called "address line", "house number and street", "road address". Examples: "The postal address has streetAddress 1600 Amphitheatre Pkwy", "The streetAddress is Main Street 123", "This address includes a streetAddress component."

candidates.label: deliveryAddress
candidates.comment: A destination relation between a parcel delivery and its destination postal address. Also called: shipping address, recipient address, delivery location. Examples: "Package" delivery address "123 Main St, Anytown, USA", "Food Order" delivery address "Apt 4B, 567 Oak Ave", "Mail" delivery address "P.O. Box 100".

candidates.label: mainContentOfPage
candidates.comment: A main content relation between a web page and the web page element that constitutes its primary subject. Also called: primary content, central element, core content. Examples: "Article Page mainContentOfPage ArticleBody", "Product Page mainContentOfPage ProductDescription", "Blog Post mainContentOfPage PostContent".

candidates.label: primaryImageOfPage
candidates.comment: A visual attribute linking a web page to its main or most prominent image. Also called main image, featured image, hero image. Examples: A web page has a primary image of page 'logo.png'. The article page has a primary image of page 'main_illustration.jpg'. The product page's primary image of page is the 'product_hero.webp'.

candidates.label: mainEntity
candidates.comment: A main entity relation between a creative work and the primary entity it describes. Also called: primary subject, about entity, central topic. Examples: "Wikipedia Article mainEntity Albert Einstein", "News Report mainEntity The Election", "Research Paper mainEntity Quantum Physics". Distinct from mainEntityOfPage, which indicates the page for which this thing is the main entity.

candidates.label: billingAddress
candidates.comment: A postal address used for billing an order. Also called: invoice address, payment address. Examples: "Order 'Online Purchase' billingAddress '123 Main St, Anytown, USA'", "Order 'Subscription' billingAddress 'PO Box 456'". Distinct from shippingAddress, which is where the item is sent.

candidates.label: originAddress
candidates.comment: The postal address of the shipper for a parcel delivery. Also called shipper address, sender's address, dispatch address. Examples: "Parcel Delivery 1 originAddress '123 Main St, Anytown'", "Shipment 2 originAddress 'Warehouse A, City B'", "Package 3 originAddress 'Sender's Home, Zip 12345'". Distinct from deliveryAddress, which is the recipient's address.

candidates.label: performers
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and its primary performers, who can be organizations or persons. Also called main artists, headliners, principal actors, featured performers. Examples: A concert has performers 'Coldplay'. A play has performers 'The Royal Shakespeare Company'. A festival has performers 'Various Artists'. Distinct from performer, which can be any performer, not necessarily the main one.

candidates.label: headline
candidates.comment: A headline relation between a creative work and its main title or headline text. Also called title, main heading, article headline. Examples: "An article has a headline 'Breaking News'.", "A creative work has a headline 'The Great Adventure'.", "The report's headline is 'Annual Review'."

relations.embedding_query_text: is_of:

instances: Spain's World Cup victory -> Spain

chosen_property.label: owns
chosen_property.justification: `owns` expresses the inverse relationship, indicating that the country owns or is associated with the World Cup triumph.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: partOfTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a trip and a larger, multi-day trip it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is a day of, is a leg of, belongs to. Examples: Day 1 of a vacation is part of the overall trip. A specific excursion is part of a larger travel itinerary. A flight segment is part of a multi-leg journey.

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: An alumni of relation between a person and an educational organization or organization they are a former student or member of. Also called graduated from, formerly attended, past affiliation. Examples: "A person is alumni of 'MIT'.", "John Doe is alumni of 'Boy Scouts of America'." Distinct from alumni, which describes the inverse relationship (organization to person).

candidates.label: memberOf
candidates.comment: A membership relation between an organization or person and the organization or program membership they belong to. Also called: belongs to, is a member of, affiliated with. Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Local Sports Club'", "Acme Corp memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Premium Membership Tier'". Distinct from member, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: recordingOf
candidates.comment: A recording of relation between a music recording and the music composition it represents. Also called rendition of, version of, based on composition. Examples: "A music recording 'Bohemian Rhapsody' is a recording of 'the Queen composition'.", "A classical track is a recording of 'Beethoven's Symphony No. 9'.", "A cover song is a recording of 'the original composition'.". Distinct from recordedAs, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: partOfEpisode
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a clip and the episode it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is featured in, belongs to, is from. Examples: A highlight reel is part of an episode. A deleted scene is part of an episode. A short preview is part of an episode.

candidates.label: isGift
candidates.comment: A transaction intent relation indicating whether an order was placed as a gift for a recipient other than the buyer. Also called gift purchase, purchased as gift, gift order. Examples: An order has isGift set to 'true'. A purchase has isGift set to 'false'. A book order has isGift set to 'true' with gift wrapping.

relations.embedding_query_text: has_winner_team:

instances: Spain's World Cup victory -> La Roja

chosen_property.label: hasWinnerTeam
chosen_property.definition: The subject event had the object sports team as its winner.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly expresses the winning team of an event.

candidates.label: winner
candidates.comment: A winner relation between a losing action and the person who won it. Also called victor, triumphant participant, successful party. Examples: ChessMatchLoseAction winner Alice, RaceLoseAction winner Bob, CompetitionLoseAction winner Charlie.

candidates.label: loser
candidates.comment: A losing participant relation between a win action and the person who lost. Also called: defeated participant, vanquished, runner-up. Examples: "Chess Match WinAction loser Opponent B", "Race WinAction loser Second Place Runner", "Debate WinAction loser Team B".

candidates.label: homeTeam
candidates.comment: A home team relation between a sports event and the team or person designated as the home participant. Also called host team, home side, local team. Examples: "A sports event has a home team 'Lions'.", "The match features a home team.", "This event's home team is a specific person."

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: awayTeam
candidates.comment: A person or sports team designated as the away team in a sports event. Also called: visiting team, opponent. Examples: "SportsEvent 'Football Match' awayTeam 'Team B'", "SportsEvent 'Basketball Game' awayTeam 'Lakers'". Distinct from homeTeam, which is the team playing at their home venue.

candidates.label: athlete
candidates.comment: A person who is a performing member of a sports team. Also called: player, team member, sportsman/sportswoman. Examples: "SportsTeam 'Lakers' athlete 'LeBron James'", "SportsTeam 'Red Sox' athlete 'Mookie Betts'", "SportsTeam 'National Team' athlete 'Megan Rapinoe'". Distinct from coach, which is a non-playing role.

candidates.label: sportsTeam
candidates.comment: A participation relation between an exercise action and the sports team involved in it. Also called "team participated", "team involved", "athletic team". Examples: "The goal was scored by the sportsTeam Real Madrid", "The race involved sportsTeam Team USA", "This action was performed by a sportsTeam.". Distinct from participant, which is a more general participant property.

candidates.label: award
candidates.comment: An award won by or for a creative work, organization, person, product, or service. Also called: honor, prize, recognition. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' award 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' award 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' award 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from awards, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: hasSponsorshipOffer
candidates.comment: A sponsorship offer relation between an event and an offer to sponsor it. Also called sponsorship opportunity, sponsor package, call for sponsors. Examples: "An event has a sponsorship offer for corporate partners.", "The conference has a sponsorship offer with different tiers.", "This festival includes a sponsorship offer.". Distinct from hasParticipationOffer, which is an offer to participate in the event.

candidates.label: awards
candidates.comment: Awards won by or for a creative work, organization, person, or product. Also called: honors, prizes, recognitions. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' awards 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' awards 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' awards 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from award, which is the singular form.
